title.zh: 卷一百七十一 列傳第一百二十一: 李渤 張仲方 裴潾 李中敏 李甘 高元裕 李漢 李景儉
title.en: Volume 171 Biographies 121: Li Bo, Zhang Zhongfang, Pei Lin, Li Zhongmin, Li Gan, Gao Yuanyu, Li Han, Li Jingjian
title.raw: 卷一百七十一 列傳第一百二十一: 李渤 張仲方 裴潾 李中敏 李甘 高元裕 李漢 李景儉 Volume 171 Biographies 121: Li Bo, Zhang Zhongfang, Pei Lin, Li Zhongmin, Li Gan, Gao Yuanyu, Li Han, Li Jingjian

sentences.zh: 李渤，字浚之，後魏橫野將軍申國公發之後。

translations.literal: Li Bo, styled Junzhi, was a descendant of Fa, Prince of Shen and General of the Transverse Field of Later Wei.
translations.idiomatic: Li Bo, courtesy name Junzhi, traced his line to Fa, Prince of Shen and General of the Transverse Field under the Northern Wei.

sentences.zh: 祖玄珪，衛尉寺主簿。

translations.literal: His grandfather was Xuan'gui, Chief Clerk of the Court of the Imperial Guard.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Xuan'gui had served as chief clerk in the Court of the Imperial Guard.

sentences.zh: 父鈞，殿中侍御史，以母喪不時舉，流於施州。

translations.literal: His father Jun was a Palace Censor; because he failed to observe the proper mourning period for his mother, he was banished to Shizhou.
translations.idiomatic: His father Jun had been a palace censor, but because he took office without completing the mourning rites for his mother, he was exiled to Shizhou.

sentences.zh: 渤恥其家汙，堅苦不仕；

translations.literal: Bo was ashamed of his family's disgrace and resolutely refused to take office;
translations.idiomatic: Bo was ashamed of the stain on his family and steadfastly refused to enter government service;

sentences.zh: 勵誌於文學，不從科舉，隱於嵩山，以讀書業文為事。

translations.literal: he devoted himself to literary study, did not follow the civil examinations, lived in seclusion on Mount Song, and made reading and writing his occupation.
translations.idiomatic: he applied himself to letters, shunned the examination track, withdrew to Mount Song, and devoted his days to reading and writing.

sentences.zh: 元和初，戶部侍郎鹽鐵轉運使李巽、諫議大夫韋況更薦之，以山人征為左拾遺。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Yuanhe era, Li Xun, Vice Minister of Revenue and Salt and Iron Transport Commissioner, and Wei Kuang, Remonstrance and Policy Advisor, repeatedly recommended him, and he was summoned as a hermit-recluse to the post of Left Reminder.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Yuanhe reign, Li Xun, vice minister of revenue and salt-and-iron transport commissioner, and Wei Kuang, remonstrance and policy advisor, recommended him again and again, until the court summoned him from reclusion to the post of Left Reminder.

sentences.zh: 渤托疾不赴，遂家東都。

translations.literal: Bo pleaded illness and did not go; he then made his home in the Eastern Capital.
translations.idiomatic: Bo pleaded illness and declined the appointment, settling instead in the Eastern Capital at Luoyang.

sentences.zh: 朝廷政有得失，附章疏陳論。

translations.literal: When there were gains or losses in court policy, he attached memorials presenting his views.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever he saw merit or fault in the court's governance, he submitted memorials setting out his views.

sentences.zh: 又撰《禦戎新錄》二十卷，表獻之。

translations.literal: He also compiled twenty volumes of New Records on Border Defense and submitted them by memorial.
translations.idiomatic: He also wrote New Records on Border Defense in twenty scrolls and presented them to the throne.

sentences.zh: 九年，以著作郎征之。

translations.literal: In the ninth year, he was summoned to the post of Gentleman of Writing.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth year of Yuanhe, he was summoned to serve as Gentleman of Writing.

sentences.zh: 詔曰：「特降新恩，用清舊議。」

translations.literal: An edict said: "A special new favor is granted, to clear away old criticism."
translations.idiomatic: The edict read: "We grant this special favor anew, that old reproaches may be laid to rest."

sentences.zh: 渤於是赴官。

translations.literal: Bo thereupon took up the office.
translations.idiomatic: Only then did Bo accept the appointment.

sentences.zh: 歲餘，遷右補闕。

translations.literal: After a year and more, he was promoted to Right Reminder.
translations.idiomatic: A little over a year later he was promoted to Right Reminder.

sentences.zh: 連上章疏忤旨，改丹王府諮議參軍，分司東都。

translations.literal: He repeatedly submitted memorials contrary to the imperial will and was reassigned as Counselor on the staff of the Prince of Dan, with duty stationed at the Eastern Capital.
translations.idiomatic: Memorial after memorial ran against the emperor's wishes, and he was reassigned as counselor to the Prince of Dan, with nominal duty at the Eastern Capital.

sentences.zh: 十二年，遷贊善大夫，依前分司。

translations.literal: In the twelfth year, he was promoted to Mentor of Heirs Apparent, retaining his Eastern Capital assignment as before.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth year he was made Mentor of Heirs Apparent, still serving in the Eastern Capital as before.

sentences.zh: 十三年，遣人上疏論時政，凡五事：一禮樂，二食貨，三刑政，四議都，五辯讎。

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year, he sent someone to submit a memorial discussing current affairs, five items in all: first ritual and music, second food and goods, third penal administration, fourth discussion of the capital, fifth distinguishing enmity.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirteenth year he had an agent submit a memorial on affairs of state in five parts: ritual and music; food and goods; penal administration; the capital; and the settling of grievances.

sentences.zh: 渤以散秩在東都，以上章疏為己任，前後四十五封。

translations.literal: Bo, holding an honorary rank in the Eastern Capital, took submitting memorials as his duty and sent forty-five in all, before and after.
translations.idiomatic: Though he held only an honorary post in the Eastern Capital, Bo made memorial-writing his calling and sent forth forty-five in all.

sentences.zh: 再遷為庫部員外郎。

translations.literal: He was promoted again to Vice Director of the Treasury Bureau.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted again, to Vice Director of the Treasury Bureau.

sentences.zh: 時皇甫镈作相，剝下希旨。

translations.literal: At the time Huangfu Bo was chancellor, oppressing the people below to win imperial favor.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Huangfu Bo was chancellor, squeezing the people to please the throne.

sentences.zh: 會澤潞節度使郗士美卒，渤充吊祭使，路次陜西。

translations.literal: When Zelu Military Commissioner Qi Shimai died, Bo was appointed envoy to offer condolences; passing through Shaanxi on the way,
translations.idiomatic: When Qi Shimai, military commissioner of Zelu, died, Bo was appointed condolence envoy; on the road through Shaanxi,

sentences.zh: 渤上疏曰：「臣出使經行，歷求利病。

translations.literal: Bo submitted a memorial saying: "Your subject, on this mission, has traveled the route and everywhere sought out benefits and harms.
translations.idiomatic: Bo submitted a memorial: "On this mission your subject has traveled the route and everywhere looked into what helps and what harms the people.

sentences.zh: 竊知渭南縣長源鄉本有四百戶，今才一百余戶；

translations.literal: I have privately learned that Changyuan township in Weinan County originally had four hundred households; now there are barely more than one hundred;
translations.idiomatic: I have learned in private that Changyuan township in Weinan County once had four hundred households; today barely more than a hundred remain;

sentences.zh: 闃鄉縣本有三千戶；

translations.literal: Qian township originally had three thousand households;
translations.idiomatic: Qian township once had three thousand households;

sentences.zh: 今才有一千戶，其他州縣大約相似。

translations.literal: now there are barely one thousand; other prefectures and counties are roughly similar.
translations.idiomatic: today barely a thousand remain, and other prefectures and counties are much the same.

sentences.zh: 訪尋積弊，始自均攤逃戶。

translations.literal: In seeking out longstanding abuses, it begins with apportioning the tax burden among escaped households.
translations.idiomatic: In tracing these chronic evils to their root, one finds the practice of spreading fugitive households' taxes among those who remain.

sentences.zh: 凡十家之內，大半逃亡，亦須五家攤稅。

translations.literal: Within any ten households, most have fled, yet five households must still share the tax.
translations.idiomatic: Of every ten households, most may have fled, yet the tax must still be shared among the five who remain.

sentences.zh: 似投石井中，非到底不止。

translations.literal: It is like throwing a stone into a well—it will not stop until it reaches the bottom.
translations.idiomatic: It is like casting a stone into a well: it does not stop until it hits bottom.

sentences.zh: 攤逃之弊，苛虐如斯，此皆聚斂之臣剝下媚上，唯思竭澤，不慮無魚。

translations.literal: The abuse of apportioning among fugitives is as harsh and cruel as this; all of this is ministers of extraction stripping those below to please those above, thinking only of draining the pond, without considering that when the pond is dry there will be no fish.
translations.idiomatic: The evil of spreading fugitives' taxes is as harsh as this. Such men are revenue-hungry ministers who strip the people to flatter their superiors, draining the pond without a thought for the day when no fish remain.

sentences.zh: 乞降詔書，絕攤逃之弊。

translations.literal: I beg that an edict be issued to abolish the abuse of apportioning among fugitives.
translations.idiomatic: I beg Your Majesty to issue an edict abolishing this practice.

sentences.zh: 其逃亡戶以其家產錢數為定，征有所欠，乞降特恩免之。

translations.literal: For fugitive households, let the tax be fixed according to the amount of their household property; for any shortfall in collection, I beg that special grace be granted to remit it.
translations.idiomatic: Let fugitive households be taxed only according to the property they left behind, and let any shortfall in collection be remitted by special grace.

sentences.zh: 計不數年，人必歸於農矣。

translations.literal: Within a few years, people will surely return to farming.
translations.idiomatic: Within a few years the people will surely return to the fields.

sentences.zh: 夫農者，國之本，本立然後可以議太平。

translations.literal: Agriculture is the foundation of the state; only when the foundation is established can one speak of great peace.
translations.idiomatic: Farming is the root of the state; only when the root is firm may one speak of great peace.

sentences.zh: 若不由茲，而雲太平者，謬矣。」

translations.literal: If one does not proceed by this path yet speaks of great peace, that is absurd."
translations.idiomatic: To speak of peace without taking this road is folly."

sentences.zh: 又言道途不修，驛馬多死。

translations.literal: He also spoke of roads not being maintained and many relay horses dying.
translations.idiomatic: He also reported that the roads were unrepaired and that relay horses were dying in great numbers.

sentences.zh: 憲宗覽疏驚異，即以飛龍馬數百匹，付畿內諸驛。

translations.literal: Emperor Xianzong read the memorial with astonishment and immediately sent several hundred Flying Dragon horses to the relay stations within the capital region.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xianzong read the memorial with alarm and at once sent several hundred Flying Dragon horses to the relay stations of the capital region.

sentences.zh: 渤既以草疏切直，大忤宰相，乃謝病東歸。

translations.literal: Since Bo's memorial had been blunt and forthright, greatly offending the chancellor, he then begged leave on grounds of illness and returned east.
translations.idiomatic: Because his blunt memorial had deeply offended the chancellor, Bo pleaded illness and withdrew eastward.

sentences.zh: 穆宗即位，召為考功員外郎。

translations.literal: When Muzong ascended the throne, he was summoned as Vice Director of the Bureau of Merit Evaluations.
translations.idiomatic: When Muzong came to the throne, Bo was recalled as Vice Director of the Bureau of Merit Evaluations.

sentences.zh: 十一月，定京官考，不避權幸，皆行升黜。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month, when the evaluations of capital officials were fixed, he did not avoid the powerful and favored, and carried out promotions and demotions for all.
translations.idiomatic: That November, when the merit reviews of capital officials were due, he spared neither the powerful nor the favored, promoting and demoting as merit required.

sentences.zh: 奏曰：

translations.literal: He submitted a memorial saying:
translations.idiomatic: He submitted a memorial that read:

sentences.zh: 宰臣蕭俛、段文昌、崔植，是陛下君臨之初，用為輔弼，安危理亂，決在此時。

translations.literal: "Chancellors Xiao Fu, Duan Wenchang, and Cui Zhi were appointed as your helpers at the beginning of your rule; whether the state is safe or endangered, well-governed or chaotic, is decided at this moment.
translations.idiomatic: "Chancellors Xiao Fu, Duan Wenchang, and Cui Zhi were chosen to assist Your Majesty at the beginning of your reign. Whether the realm stands safe or imperiled, ordered or in disorder, will be decided now.

sentences.zh: 況陛下思天下和平，敬大臣禮切，固未有昵比左右、侈滿自賢之心。

translations.literal: Moreover, Your Majesty thinks of peace under Heaven and treats great ministers with earnest respect; you clearly have no inclination to favor those at your side or to indulge in self-satisfaction at your own wisdom.
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty seeks peace for the empire and treats his ministers with sincere respect. You show no wish to cozy up to those at your side or to grow complacent in your own wisdom.

sentences.zh: 而宰相之權，宰相之事，陛下一以付之，實君義臣行，千載一遇之時也。

translations.literal: Yet the authority of the chancellors and the affairs of the chancellors Your Majesty has entirely entrusted to them—this is truly the proper conduct of ruler and subject, a moment that comes once in a thousand years.
translations.idiomatic: You have entrusted chancellors with chancellors' full authority and charge. This is the true relation of ruler and minister—a moment that comes once in a thousand years.

sentences.zh: 此時若失，他更無時。

translations.literal: If this moment is lost, there will be no other time.
translations.idiomatic: If this moment passes, there will not be another.

sentences.zh: 而俛等上不能推至公，申炯誡，陳先王道德，以沃君心；

translations.literal: Yet Fu and the others, above, cannot advance utmost impartiality, set forth clear warnings, promulgate the virtue of the former kings, and enrich the ruler's mind;
translations.idiomatic: Yet Fu and his colleagues cannot, on the one hand, press for the utmost public good, offer bright warnings, and set before you the virtue of the ancient kings to nourish your mind;

sentences.zh: 又不能正色匪躬，振舉舊法，復百司之本，俾教化大立。

translations.literal: nor below can they maintain a stern countenance and correct themselves, revive the old laws, restore the foundation of the hundred offices, and make great teaching and transformation stand firm.
translations.idiomatic: nor, on the other hand, keep stern faces, correct their own conduct, revive the old laws, restore the foundations of the hundred offices, and establish great order through teaching.

sentences.zh: 臣聞政之興廢，在於賞罰。

translations.literal: Your subject has heard that the rise and fall of government lies in rewards and punishments.
translations.idiomatic: Your subject has heard that whether government flourishes or fails depends on reward and punishment.

sentences.zh: 俛等作相已來，未聞獎一人德義，舉守官奉公者，使天下在官之徒有所激勸；

translations.literal: Since Fu and the others became chancellors, one has not heard of a single person rewarded for virtue and righteousness, or of upright officials who kept their posts and served the public being commended, so that officials throughout the realm might be stirred to emulation;
translations.idiomatic: Since Fu and the others took office, I have heard of no one rewarded for virtue, no upright official commended for keeping his post and serving the public, that officials throughout the realm might be stirred to emulation;

sentences.zh: 又不聞黜一人職事不理、持祿養驕者，使屍祿之徒有所懼。

translations.literal: nor has one heard of a single person dismissed for neglecting official duties or drawing salary while nurturing arrogance, so that those who hold office in name only might feel fear.
translations.idiomatic: nor of anyone dismissed for neglect of duty or for drawing salary while growing arrogant, that idle officeholders might feel fear.

sentences.zh: 如此，則刑法不立矣！

translations.literal: If it is like this, then penal law cannot be established!
translations.idiomatic: If matters stand thus, how can law be upheld?

sentences.zh: 邪正莫辯，混然無章，教化不行，賞罰之設，天下之事，復何望哉！

translations.literal: Wrong and right cannot be distinguished, and all is chaotic without order; teaching and transformation are not carried out—what hope is there for affairs under Heaven if rewards and punishments are set up yet nothing is done?
translations.idiomatic: Wrong cannot be told from right; all is confusion without rule; teaching goes nowhere. With reward and punishment hollow, what hope remains for the affairs of the realm?

sentences.zh: 一昨陛下遊幸驪山，宰相、翰林學士是陛下股肱心腹，宜皆知之。

translations.literal: Just yesterday Your Majesty made an excursion to Mount Li; the chancellors and Hanlin Academicians are Your Majesty's arms, legs, and inner circle—you ought to have known in advance.
translations.idiomatic: Only yesterday Your Majesty visited Mount Li. The chancellors and Hanlin academicians are your arms and your heart—they should have known beforehand.

sentences.zh: 蕭俛等不能先事未形，忘軀懇諫，而使陛下有忽諫之名流於史冊，是陷君於過也。

translations.literal: Xiao Fu and the others could not, before the matter took shape, forget themselves and remonstrate earnestly, but instead let Your Majesty acquire the name of disregarding remonstrance to flow into the historical records—this is leading the ruler into fault.
translations.idiomatic: Xiao Fu and the others failed to speak before the deed was done, forgetting themselves in earnest remonstrance, and so left Your Majesty with the name of one who ignored counsel—a stain on the historical record and a fault into which ministers lead their ruler.

sentences.zh: 孔子曰：「所謂大臣者，以道事君，不可則止。」

translations.literal: Confucius said: "What is called a great minister serves the ruler by the Way; if this cannot be done, he stops."
translations.idiomatic: Confucius said, "What is called a great minister serves his ruler by the Way; if that cannot be done, he withdraws."

sentences.zh: 若俛等言行計從，不當如是。

translations.literal: If Fu and the others' words and deeds were heeded, they ought not to have acted thus.
translations.idiomatic: If Fu and the others had truly been heeded in word and deed, they should not have acted as they did.

sentences.zh: 若言不行，計不從，須奉身速退，不宜屍素於化源。

translations.literal: If their words were not heeded and their plans not followed, they ought quickly to withdraw and offer themselves, and ought not to hold empty positions at the source of transformation.
translations.idiomatic: If their words went unheeded and their plans unfollowed, they should have withdrawn at once and not clung to empty posts at the very source of government.

sentences.zh: 進退戾也，何所避辭？

translations.literal: Their advance and retreat were perverse—what is there to shirk in saying so?
translations.idiomatic: In advance and retreat they were perverse. What excuse is there for holding back the truth?

sentences.zh: 其蕭亻免、段文昌、崔植三人並翰林學士杜元穎等，並請考中下。

translations.literal: I request that Xiao Fu, Duan Wenchang, and Cui Zhi, together with Hanlin Academician Du Yuanying and others, all be given middle-lower evaluations.
translations.idiomatic: I therefore ask that Xiao Fu, Duan Wenchang, and Cui Zhi, together with Hanlin Academician Du Yuanying and others, all be rated middle-lower.

sentences.zh: 御史大夫李絳、左散騎常侍張惟素、右散騎常侍李益等諫幸驪山，鄭覃等諫畋遊，是皆恐陛下行幸不息，恣情無度；

translations.literal: Censor-in-Chief Li Jiang, Left Regular Attendant of the Right Cavalry Zhang Weisu, Right Regular Attendant of the Right Cavalry Li Yi, and others remonstrated against the excursion to Mount Li; Zheng Tan and others remonstrated against hunting excursions—all because they feared Your Majesty's travel would never cease and your indulgence would know no bounds;
translations.idiomatic: Censor-in-Chief Li Jiang, Left Regular Attendant Zhang Weisu, Right Regular Attendant Li Yi, and others remonstrated against the visit to Mount Li; Zheng Tan and others remonstrated against hunting—all fearing that Your Majesty's travels would never end and your pleasures know no limit;

sentences.zh: 又恐馬有銜蹶不測之變，風寒生疾之憂，急奏無所詣，國璽委於婦人中幸之手。

translations.literal: they also feared unforeseeable mishaps if the horses bolted or stumbled, and the worry of illness from wind and cold; urgent memorials had nowhere to go, and the imperial seal was placed in the hands of palace women and favored attendants.
translations.idiomatic: they feared as well the unforeseeable accident of a runaway or stumbling horse, the chill wind and sickness it might bring, the lack of any channel for urgent memorials, and the imperial seal left in the hands of palace women and favored attendants.

sentences.zh: 絳等能率御史諫官論列於朝，有懇激事君之體。

translations.literal: Jiang and the others were able to lead censors and remonstrance officials to discuss matters openly at court—they had the proper bearing of earnest and impassioned service to the ruler.
translations.idiomatic: Jiang and the others led the censors and remonstrance officials in open debate at court, showing the earnest, impassioned bearing of true service to the ruler.

sentences.zh: 其李絳、張惟素、李益三人，伏請賜上下考外，特與遷官，以彰陛下優忠賞諫之美。

translations.literal: As for Li Jiang, Zhang Weisu, and Li Yi, I humbly request that, in addition to giving them upper-middle evaluations, they be specially granted promotions, to display Your Majesty's beauty in honoring loyalty and rewarding remonstrance.
translations.idiomatic: As for Li Jiang, Zhang Weisu, and Li Yi, I humbly ask that beyond an upper-middle rating they be specially promoted, that Your Majesty's grace toward loyalty and reward for remonstrance may be made plain.

sentences.zh: 其崔元略冠供奉之首，合考上下；

translations.literal: As for Cui Yuanlue, he heads the Palace Attendants and ought to receive an upper-middle evaluation;
translations.idiomatic: Cui Yuanlue, who heads the palace attendants, merits an upper-middle rating;

sentences.zh: 緣與於翚上下考，於翚以犯贓處死，準令須降，請賜考中中。

translations.literal: because he shares an upper-middle evaluation with Yu Hui, and Yu Hui was executed for corruption, under the regulations the evaluation must be lowered—I request that he be given a middle evaluation.
translations.idiomatic: but because he was rated upper-middle together with Yu Hui, and Yu Hui was executed for corruption, the regulations require a reduction. I ask that he be rated middle.

sentences.zh: 大理卿許季同，任使於翚、韋道沖、韋正牧，皆以犯贓，或左降，或處死，合考中下；

translations.literal: Chief Minister of Justice Xu Jitong, in appointing Yu Hui, Wei Daochong, and Wei Zhengmu, all of whom were guilty of corruption and were either demoted or executed, ought to receive a middle-lower evaluation;
translations.idiomatic: Chief Minister of Justice Xu Jitong, who appointed Yu Hui, Wei Daochong, and Wei Zhengmu—all convicted of corruption and either demoted or executed—merits a middle-lower rating;

sentences.zh: 然頃者陷劉辟之亂，棄家歸朝，忠節明著，今宜以功補過，請賜考中中。

translations.literal: yet recently, when caught in Liu Pi's rebellion, he abandoned his family and returned to court—his loyalty and integrity were clear; now his merit should offset his fault, and I request that he be given a middle evaluation.
translations.idiomatic: yet when Liu Pi's rebellion engulfed the region, he abandoned his family and returned to court, his loyalty plain for all to see. His merit should now offset his fault. I ask that he be rated middle.

sentences.zh: 少府監裴通，職事修舉，合考中上；

translations.literal: Director of the Palace Manufactories Pei Tong has managed his duties well and ought to receive a middle-upper evaluation;
translations.idiomatic: Pei Tong, Director of the Palace Manufactories, has performed his duties well and merits a middle-upper rating;

sentences.zh: 以其請追封所生母而舍嫡母，是明罔於君，幽欺其先，請考中下。

translations.literal: because he requested posthumous ennoblement for his birth mother while setting aside his legal wife-mother, clearly deceiving the ruler in the open and secretly deceiving his ancestors—I request a middle-lower evaluation.
translations.idiomatic: but because he sought posthumous honors for his birth mother while setting aside his legal mother, openly deceiving the ruler and secretly wronging his ancestors, I ask a middle-lower rating.

sentences.zh: 伏以昔在宰夫入寢，擅飲師曠、李調。

translations.literal: I humbly reflect that in ancient times a cook entered the sleeping chamber and drank from the flasks of Shi Kuang and Li Diao without permission.
translations.idiomatic: I recall that in antiquity a cook entered the sleeping chamber and drank from the cups of Shi Kuang and Li Diao without leave.

sentences.zh: 今愚臣守官，請書宰相學士中下考。

translations.literal: Today this foolish official, keeping his post, requests to enter middle-lower evaluations for the chancellors and academicians.
translations.idiomatic: Today this humble official, merely doing his duty, asks leave to record middle-lower ratings for the chancellors and academicians.

sentences.zh: 上愛聖運，下振頹綱，故臣懼不言之為罪，不懼言之為罪也。

translations.literal: Honoring the sacred destiny above and restoring the failing framework below—therefore your subject fears that not speaking would be a crime, and does not fear that speaking would be a crime.
translations.idiomatic: Out of love for the sacred age above and desire to revive the failing order below, your subject fears the crime of silence, not the crime of speech.

sentences.zh: 其三品官考，伏緣限在今月內進，輒先具如前。

translations.literal: As for the evaluations of third-rank officials, because the deadline for submission falls within this month, I venture to set them forth in advance as above.
translations.idiomatic: Because the deadline for third-rank evaluations falls within this month, I venture to submit these ratings in advance as above.

sentences.zh: 其四品以下官，續具條疏聞奏。

translations.literal: For officials of the fourth rank and below, I shall continue to set them forth in detail and report them by memorial.
translations.idiomatic: Ratings for officials of the fourth rank and below I shall continue to set forth in detail in a further memorial.

sentences.zh: 狀入，留中不下。

translations.literal: When the report was submitted, it was kept in the palace and not issued.
translations.idiomatic: When the report reached the throne, it was kept within and never promulgated.

sentences.zh: 議者以宰輔曠官，自宜上疏論列，而渤越職釣名，非盡事君之道。

translations.literal: Commentators held that the chancellors' neglect of office ought indeed to have been criticized in memorials, but that Bo had overstepped his duties and fished for reputation—not fully the way of serving a ruler.
translations.idiomatic: Critics agreed that the chancellors' neglect of duty deserved open criticism, but held that Bo had overstepped his office and courted fame—not the whole of a minister's duty to his ruler.

sentences.zh: 未幾，渤以墜馬傷足，請告，會魏博節度使田弘正表渤為副使。

translations.literal: Before long, Bo injured his foot in a fall from a horse and requested leave; it happened that Weibo Military Commissioner Tian Hongzheng memorialized recommending Bo as deputy commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: Before long Bo injured his foot in a fall from his horse and asked for leave; at the same time Tian Hongzheng, military commissioner of Weibo, memorialized recommending Bo as his deputy.

sentences.zh: 杜元穎奏曰：「渤賣直沽名，動多狂躁。

translations.literal: Du Yuanying submitted a memorial saying: "Bo sells uprightness to buy a name; his conduct is often rash and reckless.
translations.idiomatic: Du Yuanying submitted a memorial: "Bo peddles integrity for reputation; his conduct is often rash and unsteady.

sentences.zh: 聖恩矜貸，且使居官。

translations.literal: Through imperial grace and forbearance he was still allowed to hold office.
translations.idiomatic: By imperial grace he was spared and allowed to remain in office.

sentences.zh: 而幹進多端，外交方鎮，遠求奏請，不能自安。

translations.literal: Yet he aggressively seeks advancement by many means, maintains outside contacts with regional commanders, and sends distant petitions—he cannot settle down.
translations.idiomatic: Yet he schemes for advancement by every path, cultivates ties with regional commanders, and sends petitions from afar. He cannot rest content.

sentences.zh: 久留在朝，轉恐生事。」

translations.literal: If he remains long at court, I fear trouble will arise."
translations.idiomatic: If he stays long at court, I fear he will make trouble."

sentences.zh: 乃出為虔州刺史。

translations.literal: He was therefore sent out as Prefect of Qianzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Bo was therefore sent out to serve as prefect of Qianzhou.

sentences.zh: 渤至州，奏還鄰境信州所移兩稅錢二百萬，免稅米二萬斛，減所由一千六百人。

translations.literal: When Bo arrived at the prefecture, he memorialized to return two million in liangshui tax funds transferred from neighboring Xinzhou, exempted twenty thousand bushels of tax grain, and reduced the subordinate staff by sixteen hundred persons.
translations.idiomatic: On reaching Qianzhou, Bo memorialized to return two million in liangshui tax monies shifted from neighboring Xinzhou, exempted twenty thousand bushels of tax grain, and cut sixteen hundred subordinate staff.

sentences.zh: 觀察使以其事上聞。

translations.literal: The surveillance commissioner reported these matters to the throne.
translations.idiomatic: The surveillance commissioner reported these measures to the throne.

sentences.zh: 未滿歲，遷江州刺史。

translations.literal: Before a full year had passed, he was transferred to Prefect of Jiangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Before a year was out he was transferred to prefect of Jiangzhou.

sentences.zh: 張平叔判度支，奏征久遠逋懸，渤在州上疏曰：「伏奉詔敕，雲度支使所奏，令臣設計征填當州貞元二年逃戶所欠錢四千四百一十貫。

translations.literal: Zhang Pingshu, acting Director of the Revenue Bureau, memorialized to collect long-standing overdue taxes; Bo, while prefect, submitted a memorial saying: "I humbly received the edict stating that the Director of the Revenue Bureau has memorialized ordering me to devise means to collect and make up the 4,410 strings owed by fugitive households of the second year of the Zhenyuan era in this prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Pingshu, acting director of the Revenue Bureau, memorialized to collect long-overdue taxes. From Jiangzhou Bo submitted a memorial: "I have received the edict reporting the Revenue Bureau's request that I devise means to collect the 4,410 strings still owed by fugitive households from the second year of the Zhenyuan era in this prefecture.

sentences.zh: 臣當州管田二千一百九十七頃，今已旱死一千九百頃有余，若更勒徇度支使所為，必懼史官書陛下於大旱中征三十六年前逋懸。

translations.literal: Your subject's prefecture administers 2,197 qing of fields; more than 1,900 qing have already died from drought; if I further compelled compliance with what the Director of the Revenue Bureau has done, I would surely fear that the historians would record that Your Majesty collected thirty-six-year-old arrears in the midst of great drought.
translations.idiomatic: This prefecture oversees 2,197 qing of fields; more than 1,900 qing have already withered in drought. If I were forced to obey the Revenue Bureau, I would fear the historians would write that Your Majesty collected thirty-six-year-old arrears in the midst of great drought.

sentences.zh: 臣任刺史，罪無所逃。

translations.literal: As prefect I cannot escape blame.
translations.idiomatic: As prefect I cannot escape blame for what follows.

sentences.zh: 臣既上不副聖情，下不忍鞭笞黎庶，不敢輕持符印，特乞放臣歸田。」

translations.literal: Your subject can neither meet the imperial intent above nor bear to lash the common people below; I dare not lightly hold the seal and commission, and specially beg to be released to return to my fields."
translations.idiomatic: I can neither satisfy the throne above nor bear to flog the people below. I dare not lightly keep seal and commission in hand, and beg to be released to return to my fields."

sentences.zh: 乃下詔曰：「江州所奏，實為懇誠。

translations.literal: An edict was then issued saying: "What Jiangzhou has memorialized is truly earnest and sincere.
translations.idiomatic: The court then issued an edict: "Jiangzhou's memorial is truly earnest.

sentences.zh: 若不蠲容，必難存濟。

translations.literal: If relief is not granted, survival will surely be impossible.
translations.idiomatic: Without remission the people cannot survive.

sentences.zh: 所訴逋欠並放。」

translations.literal: All the overdue debts complained of are remitted."
translations.idiomatic: All the overdue debts described are remitted."

sentences.zh: 長慶二年，入為職方郎中。

translations.literal: In the second year of Changqing, he entered court as Director of the Bureau of Titles and Patents.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Changqing he returned to court as Director of the Bureau of Titles and Patents.

sentences.zh: 三年，遷諫議大夫。

translations.literal: In the third year, he was promoted to Remonstrance and Policy Advisor.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year he was promoted to Remonstrance and Policy Advisor.

sentences.zh: 長慶、寶歷中，政出多門，事歸邪幸。

translations.literal: During the Changqing and Baoli eras, policy issued from many gates and affairs fell into the hands of wicked favorites.
translations.idiomatic: Through the Changqing and Baoli reigns power leaked through many doors, and affairs fell to wicked favorites.

sentences.zh: 渤不顧忠難，章疏論列，曾無虛日。

translations.literal: Bo disregarded the danger to his loyalty and discussed matters in memorial after memorial—hardly a day passed without one.
translations.idiomatic: Bo ignored the peril to himself and memorialized without cease—scarcely a day passed without a submission.

sentences.zh: 帝雖昏縱，亦為之感悟。

translations.literal: Though the emperor was muddled and indulgent, he was moved by this nonetheless.
translations.idiomatic: Though the emperor was dull and self-indulgent, even he was moved.

sentences.zh: 轉給事中，面賜金紫。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Supervising Censor and was personally granted the gold seal and purple robe in audience.
translations.idiomatic: He was made Supervising Censor and in audience was personally granted the gold seal and purple robe.

sentences.zh: 寶歷元年，改元大赦。

translations.literal: In the first year of Baoli, the era name was changed and a general amnesty was proclaimed.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Baoli the reign title was changed and a general amnesty was proclaimed.

sentences.zh: 先是，鄠縣令崔發聞門外喧鬥，縣吏言五坊使下毆擊百姓。

translations.literal: Previously, Magistrate Cui Fa of Hu County heard a noisy brawl outside the gate; a county clerk said that men from the Five Offices commissioners below were beating common people.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, Cui Fa, magistrate of Hu County, heard a noisy brawl outside the gate. A clerk reported that men sent by the Five Offices commissioners were beating common people.

sentences.zh: 發怒，命吏捕之。

translations.literal: Fa grew angry and ordered clerks to arrest them.
translations.idiomatic: Fa flew into a rage and ordered his clerks to seize them.

sentences.zh: 曳挾既至，時已曛黑，不問色目。

translations.literal: When they were dragged in, it was already dusk; he did not ask who they were.
translations.idiomatic: When the men were dragged in, night had already fallen, and he did not ask who they were.

sentences.zh: 良久與語，乃知是一內官。

translations.literal: After speaking at length, he learned that the man was an imperial eunuch.
translations.idiomatic: Only after talking at length did he learn the man was an imperial eunuch.

sentences.zh: 天子聞之怒，收發系御史臺。

translations.literal: When the Son of Heaven heard of it he grew angry; Cui Fa was arrested and imprisoned at the Bureau of Investigation.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor heard of it he flew into a rage, had Cui Fa arrested, and imprisoned him at the imperial censorate.

sentences.zh: 禦樓之日，放系囚，發亦在雞竿下。

translations.literal: On the day of the imperial tower audience, confined prisoners were released; Fa was also beneath the cock pole.
translations.idiomatic: On the day of the imperial tower amnesty, prisoners in confinement were released—and Fa stood beneath the pardon pole as well.

sentences.zh: 時有品官五十余人，持仗毆發，縱橫亂擊，發破面折齒。

translations.literal: At the time more than fifty ranked officials, wielding staffs, beat Fa, striking wildly; Fa's face was torn and his teeth broken.
translations.idiomatic: At the time more than fifty ranked officials, wielding clubs, beat Fa in a wild frenzy; his face was torn open and his teeth were broken.

sentences.zh: 臺吏以席蔽之，方免。

translations.literal: Censorate clerks shielded him with mats before he escaped harm.
translations.idiomatic: Censorate clerks covered him with mats before he was spared further injury.

sentences.zh: 是日系囚皆釋，發獨不免。

translations.literal: That day all confined prisoners were released; Fa alone was not freed.
translations.idiomatic: That day every confined prisoner was released; Fa alone was not freed.

sentences.zh: 渤疏論之曰：「縣令不合曳中人，中人不合毆禦囚，其罪一也。

translations.literal: Bo submitted a memorial discussing it, saying: "The magistrate should not have dragged an imperial attendant; the attendant should not have beaten a prisoner under imperial amnesty—their offense is one and the same.
translations.idiomatic: Bo submitted a memorial arguing: "The magistrate should not have dragged an imperial attendant, and the attendant should not have beaten a prisoner under imperial amnesty—the fault is the same in both.

sentences.zh: 然縣令所犯在恩前，中人所犯在恩後。

translations.literal: Yet the magistrate's offense came before the amnesty, while the attendant's came after it.
translations.idiomatic: Yet the magistrate's offense occurred before the amnesty, while the attendant's occurred after it.

sentences.zh: 中人橫暴，一至於此，是朝廷馴致使然。

translations.literal: That imperial attendants should be so violent and overbearing is something the court has tamed and allowed.
translations.idiomatic: That imperial attendants should be so violent and overbearing shows how the court has indulged and trained them to it.

sentences.zh: 若不早正刑書，臣恐四夷之人及籓鎮奏事傳道此語，則慢易之心萌矣。」

translations.literal: If the penal code is not applied soon, I fear that foreigners and frontier commanders reporting affairs will hear this tale and contempt will take root."
translations.idiomatic: If punishment is not imposed at once, I fear that foreigners and frontier commanders who hear this tale will take it as license for contempt."

sentences.zh: 渤又宣言於朝云：「郊禮前一日，兩神策軍於青城內奪京兆府進食牙盤，不時處置，致有毆擊崔發之事。」

translations.literal: Bo also declared at court: "On the day before the suburban sacrifice, two Shence Army units inside the Green City seized the tooth-trays of food presented by the Jingzhao prefecture; because the matter was not handled promptly, the beating of Cui Fa ensued."
translations.idiomatic: Bo also proclaimed at court: "On the eve of the suburban sacrifice, two Shence Army units inside the Green City seized the serving trays of food presented by the Jingzhao prefecture; because the matter was not dealt with in time, the beating of Cui Fa followed."

sentences.zh: 上聞之，按問左右，皆言無奪食事。

translations.literal: When the emperor heard this, he questioned those around him; all said there had been no seizure of food.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor heard this, he questioned those around him; all denied any seizure of food.

sentences.zh: 以渤黨發，出為桂州刺史、兼御史中丞，充桂管都防禦觀察使。

translations.literal: Because Bo sided with Fa, he was sent out as prefect of Guizhou and concurrent Vice Censor-in-Chief, serving as Guiguan defense and observation commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: Deeming Bo partisan toward Fa, the court sent him out as prefect of Guizhou and concurrent vice censor-in-chief, with charge as Guiguan defense and observation commissioner.

sentences.zh: 渤雖被斥，正論不已，而諫官繼論其屈。

translations.literal: Though Bo was dismissed, he did not cease his upright arguments, and remonstrance officials continued to plead that he had been wronged.
translations.idiomatic: Though dismissed, Bo never ceased his upright arguments, and remonstrance officials continued to argue that he had been wronged.

sentences.zh: 後宰相李逢吉、竇易直、李程因延英上語及崔發，逢吉等奏曰：「崔發淩轢中人，誠大不敬。

translations.literal: Later the chief ministers Li Fengji, Dou Yizhi, and Li Cheng, while speaking with the emperor at Yanying, mentioned Cui Fa; Fengji and the others memorialized: "Cui Fa insulted and trampled upon an imperial attendant—truly a grave lack of respect.
translations.idiomatic: Later, when chief ministers Li Fengji, Dou Yizhi, and Li Cheng spoke with the emperor at Yanying and mentioned Cui Fa, Fengji and the others memorialized: "Cui Fa insulted and trampled upon an imperial attendant—a grave lack of respect.

sentences.zh: 然發母是故相韋貫之姊，年僅八十。

translations.literal: Yet Fa's mother is the elder sister of the former chief minister Wei Guanzhi and is nearly eighty.
translations.idiomatic: Yet Fa's mother is the elder sister of the former chief minister Wei Guanzhi and is nearly eighty years old.

sentences.zh: 自發下獄，積憂成疾。

translations.literal: Since Fa was imprisoned, worry piled up into illness.
translations.idiomatic: Since Fa was imprisoned, worry had piled up into illness.

sentences.zh: 伏以陛下孝治天下，稍垂恩宥。」

translations.literal: I submit that Your Majesty governs the realm through filial piety; grant a little mercy and pardon."
translations.idiomatic: I submit that Your Majesty governs the realm through filial piety; may you show a little mercy and pardon."

sentences.zh: 帝湣然良久，曰：「比諫官論奏，但言發屈，未嘗言不敬之罪，亦不言有老母。

translations.literal: The emperor was moved for a long while and said: "When remonstrance officials spoke lately, they only said Fa had been wronged; they never mentioned the crime of disrespect, nor that he had an aged mother.
translations.idiomatic: For a long while the emperor was visibly moved and said: "When remonstrance officials spoke lately, they spoke only of Fa's wronged treatment; never once named the offense of disrespect, nor noted that he had an aged mother.

sentences.zh: 如卿等言，寧無湣惻！」

translations.literal: As you describe it, how could I not feel compassion!"
translations.idiomatic: Hearing you put it so, how could I not feel pity!"

sentences.zh: 即遣中使送發至其家，兼撫問發母。

translations.literal: He immediately sent palace envoys to escort Fa home and also to console Fa's mother.
translations.idiomatic: At once he dispatched palace envoys to escort Fa home and sent others to comfort Fa's mother.

sentences.zh: 韋夫人號哭，對中使杖發四十，拜章謝恩。

translations.literal: Madame Wei wailed and, before the envoys, had Fa beaten forty strokes with the staff, then submitted a memorial thanking the grace.
translations.idiomatic: Madame Wei wailed and, before the envoys, had Fa beaten forty strokes with the staff, then submitted a memorial thanking the emperor's grace.

sentences.zh: 帝又遣中使慰安之。

translations.literal: The emperor again sent palace envoys to comfort her.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor once more sent palace envoys to offer her consolation.

sentences.zh: 渤在桂管二年，風恙求代，罷歸洛陽。

translations.literal: Bo spent two years in Guiguan, then sought a replacement because of wind ailment and returned to Luoyang.
translations.idiomatic: After two years in Guiguan, Bo sought relief from his post because of a wind ailment and withdrew to Luoyang.

sentences.zh: 太和五年，以太子賓客征至京師。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Taihe he was summoned to the capital as Grand Mentor of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year of Taihe he was summoned to the capital as grand mentor of the heir apparent.

sentences.zh: 月余卒，時年五十九，贈禮部尚書。

translations.literal: After a little more than a month he died, aged fifty-nine; he was posthumously made Minister of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: After a little more than a month he died, aged fifty-nine; he was posthumously made minister of rites.

sentences.zh: 渤孤貞，力行操尚，不茍合，而阘茸之流，非其沽激。

translations.literal: Bo was solitary and upright, forceful in conduct and principle, unwilling to compromise; vulgar mediocrities were not his sort of moral posturing.
translations.idiomatic: Bo was solitary and upright, forceful in conduct and unwilling to compromise; vulgar mediocrities were not the audience for his moral zeal.

sentences.zh: 至於以言擯退，終不息言，以救時病，服名節者重之。

translations.literal: Though driven from office for his words, he never ceased speaking, seeking to remedy the ills of the age; men who valued integrity esteemed him.
translations.idiomatic: Though driven from office for his words, he never ceased speaking to remedy the ills of the age; men who valued integrity esteemed him.

sentences.zh: 子祝，會昌中登進士第，辟諸侯府。

translations.literal: His son Zhu passed the civil examinations in the Huichang era and entered the staff of a regional lord.
translations.idiomatic: His son Zhu earned his jinshi degree in the Huichang era and entered the staff of a regional lord.

sentences.zh: 張仲方，韶州始興人。

translations.literal: Zhang Zhongfang was a native of Shixing in Shaozhou.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Zhongfang hailed from Shixing in Shaozhou.

sentences.zh: 祖九臯，廣州刺史、殿中監、嶺南節度使。

translations.literal: His grandfather Jiugao was prefect of Guangzhou, Director of the Palace Domestic Service, and military commissioner of Lingnan.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Jiugao was prefect of Guangzhou, director of the palace domestic service, and military commissioner of Lingnan.

sentences.zh: 父抗，贈右僕射。

translations.literal: His father Kang was posthumously made Right Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: His father Kang was posthumously made right vice director of the Department of State Affairs.

sentences.zh: 仲方伯祖始興文獻公九齡，開元朝名相。

translations.literal: Zhongfang's great-uncle Jiuling, Duke Wenxian of Shixing, was a famed chief minister of the Kaiyuan reign.
translations.idiomatic: Zhongfang's great-uncle Jiuling, Duke Wenxian of Shixing, had been a celebrated chief minister under Kaiyuan.

sentences.zh: 仲方，貞元中進士擢第，宏辭登科，釋褐集賢校理，丁母憂免。

translations.literal: Zhongfang passed the civil examinations in the Zhenyuan era and also passed the macro-elocution examination; upon leaving office he became collator in the Palace Library and left service for mourning his mother.
translations.idiomatic: Zhongfang passed the civil examinations in the Zhenyuan era and also passed the macro-elocution examination; upon leaving office he became collator in the Palace Library, then left service to mourn his mother.

sentences.zh: 服闋，補秘書省正字，調授咸陽尉。

translations.literal: When mourning ended he was made proofreader in the Secretariat and transferred to be magistrate of Xianyang.
translations.idiomatic: Once mourning was complete he became a proofreader in the Secretariat, then was transferred to magistrate of Xianyang.

sentences.zh: 出為邠州從事，入朝歷侍御史、倉部員外郎。

translations.literal: He went out as aide in Binzhou and on entering court served successively as investigating censor and vice director of the granaries bureau.
translations.idiomatic: He served as an aide in Binzhou, then on entering court rose through investigating censor to vice director of the granaries bureau.

sentences.zh: 會呂溫、羊士諤誣告宰相李吉甫陰事，二人俱貶。

translations.literal: When Lü Wen and Yang Shifu falsely accused Chief Minister Li Jifu of secret matters, both were demoted.
translations.idiomatic: When Lü Wen and Yang Shifu falsely accused chief minister Li Jifu of secret dealings, both men were demoted.

sentences.zh: 仲方坐呂溫貢舉門生，出為金州刺史。

translations.literal: Zhongfang, implicated as a examination protégé of Lü Wen, was sent out as prefect of Jinzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Zhongfang, implicated as an examination protégé of Lü Wen, was sent out as prefect of Jinzhou.

sentences.zh: 吉甫卒，入為度支郎中。

translations.literal: When Jifu died, Zhongfang entered court as director of the revenue bureau.
translations.idiomatic: After Jifu's death, Zhongfang entered court as director of the revenue bureau.

sentences.zh: 時太常定吉甫謚為「恭懿」，博士尉遲汾請為「敬憲」，仲方駁議曰：

translations.literal: At the time the Court of Imperial Sacrifices fixed Jifu's posthumous title as "Respectful and Virtuous"; Erudite Yuchi Fen requested "Reverent and Lawful"; Zhongfang rebutted in a memorial, saying:
translations.idiomatic: The Court of Imperial Sacrifices had fixed Jifu's posthumous title as "Respectful and Virtuous"; erudite Yuchi Fen proposed "Reverent and Lawful"; Zhongfang answered in a memorial:

sentences.zh: 古者，易名請謚，禮之典也。

translations.literal: In antiquity, changing the name and requesting a posthumous title was a ritual norm.
translations.idiomatic: In ancient times, to change a name and petition a posthumous title was a ritual norm.

sentences.zh: 處大位者，取其巨節，蔑諸細行，垂範當代，昭示後人，然後書之，垂於不朽。

translations.literal: One who holds great position should be judged by his major integrity, with minor conduct set aside, setting an example for the age and showing posterity—only then is it written and made immortal.
translations.idiomatic: One who holds high office should be judged by his great integrity, not petty lapses, so that he may stand as an example to the age and a lesson to posterity—only then should the record be written and made enduring.

sentences.zh: 善善惡惡，不可以誣，故稱一字，則至明矣；

translations.literal: Praising good and condemning evil must not be falsified; thus a single character makes the judgment utterly clear;
translations.idiomatic: Praise and blame must not be falsified; a single character should make the judgment unmistakable;

sentences.zh: 定褒貶是非之宜，泯同異紛綸之論。

translations.literal: it fixes the measure of praise and blame, right and wrong, and stills the tangle of conflicting opinion.
translations.idiomatic: it fixes the measure of right and wrong and stills the tangle of conflicting opinion.

sentences.zh: 贈司徒吉甫，稟氣生材，乘時佐治，博涉多藝，含章炳文。

translations.literal: The late Minister of Works Jifu received heaven's endowment and born talent, seized the moment to aid governance, broadly mastered many arts, and bore luminous literary grace.
translations.idiomatic: The late minister of works Jifu was heaven-endowed and talented, seized the moment to aid governance, mastered many arts, and bore luminous literary grace.

sentences.zh: 燮贊陰陽，經緯邦國。

translations.literal: He harmonized yin and yang and wove the fabric of the state.
translations.idiomatic: He harmonized yin and yang and wove the fabric of the state together.

sentences.zh: 惜乎通敏資性，便媚取容。

translations.literal: Alas, by nature clever and quick, he fawned and sought favor.
translations.idiomatic: Yet by nature he was clever and quick, fawning on others and currying favor.

sentences.zh: 故載踐樞衡，疊致臺袞，大權在己，沈謀罕成，好惡徇情，輕諾寡信。

translations.literal: Thus he repeatedly tread the hubs of power and piled up ministerial rank; great authority rested in himself, deep plans rarely succeeded, likes and dislikes followed private feeling, light promises and scant faith.
translations.idiomatic: Thus he repeatedly tread the hubs of power and piled up ministerial rank; great authority rested with him, deep plans rarely succeeded, private feeling guided likes and dislikes, and promises came lightly while faith ran thin.

sentences.zh: 諂淚在臉，遇便則流；

translations.literal: Flattery showed on his face and flowed when it served him;
translations.idiomatic: Flattery sat on his face and flowed whenever it served him;

sentences.zh: 巧言如簧，應機必發。

translations.literal: clever words like reeds sounded whenever occasion demanded.
translations.idiomatic: clever words like reeds sounded whenever occasion arose.

sentences.zh: 夫人臣之翼戴元後者，端恪致治，孜孜夙夜，絹熙庶績，平章百揆。

translations.literal: As for a minister who supports the sovereign, he should be upright and diligent in bringing order, toiling from dawn to dusk, brightening the multitude of tasks and harmonizing the hundred offices.
translations.idiomatic: A minister who supports the sovereign should be upright and tireless in bringing order, toiling from dawn to dusk, brightening the multitude of tasks and harmonizing the hundred offices.

sentences.zh: 兵者兇器，不可從我始；

translations.literal: Arms are instruments of violence; one must not be the first to wield them from oneself;
translations.idiomatic: Arms are instruments of violence; one must not be first to take them up on one's own account;

sentences.zh: 及乎伐罪，則料敵以成功。

translations.literal: when punishing guilt, one gauges the enemy to achieve success.
translations.idiomatic: when punishing the guilty, one gauges the enemy to achieve success.

sentences.zh: 至使內有害輔臣之盜，外有懷毒蠆之孽。

translations.literal: Yet within there were thieves harming assisting ministers, and without there were venomous evils harboring poison.
translations.idiomatic: Yet within, thieves harmed assisting ministers; without, venomous evils harbored poison.

sentences.zh: 師徒暴野，戎馬生郊。

translations.literal: Armies ravaged the wilds and war horses bred in the suburbs.
translations.idiomatic: Armies ravaged the countryside and war horses foaled in the suburbs.

sentences.zh: 皇上旰食宵衣，公卿大夫且慚且恥。

translations.literal: The emperor skipped meals and rose at night; grandees and high officials felt shame together.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor skipped meals and rose at night; grandees and high officials alike burned with shame.

sentences.zh: 農人不得在畝，緝婦不得在桑。

translations.literal: Farmers could not work the furrows; women who reel silk could not be at the mulberry.
translations.idiomatic: Farmers could not work the furrows; women who reel silk could not tend the mulberry.

sentences.zh: 耗斂賦之常貲，散帑廩之中積；

translations.literal: Regular tax levies were drained and treasury stores scattered;
translations.idiomatic: Ordinary tax levies were drained dry and treasury stores scattered;

sentences.zh: 征邊僥之備，竭運挽之勞。

translations.literal: border defense reserves were exhausted and transport labor worn out.
translations.idiomatic: border defense reserves were exhausted and transport labor worn to the bone.

sentences.zh: 僵屍血流，胔骼成嶽，酷毒之痛，號訴無辜，剿絕群生，逮今四載。

translations.literal: Corpses and flowing blood piled like hills; the pain of cruel slaughter cried out from the innocent; life was cut off for four years to this day.
translations.idiomatic: Corpses and flowing blood piled like hills; the agony of cruel slaughter cried out from the innocent; life had been cut off for four years to this day.

sentences.zh: 禍胎之兆，實始其謀；

translations.literal: The omen of disaster in truth began in his scheming;
translations.idiomatic: The omen of disaster truly began in his scheming;

sentences.zh: 遺君父之憂，而豈謂之先覺者乎？

translations.literal: he left worry to ruler and father—yet can this be called foresight?
translations.idiomatic: he bequeathed worry to ruler and father—yet can such a man be called prescient?

sentences.zh: 夫論大功者，不可以妄取，不可以枉致。

translations.literal: In judging great merit, one must not seize it rashly or gain it by bending the truth.
translations.idiomatic: In judging great merit, one must not seize it rashly or gain it by bending truth.

sentences.zh: 為資畫者體理，不顯不競，而豈妨令美？

translations.literal: To plan for the state's structure without display or rivalry—how could that hinder a fair reputation?
translations.idiomatic: To plan for the state's structure without display or rivalry—how could that tarnish a fair reputation?

sentences.zh: 當削平西蜀，乃言語侍從之臣；

translations.literal: When the west in Shu was pacified, he was but a member of the literary entourage;
translations.idiomatic: When Shu in the west was pacified, he was only a member of the literary entourage;

sentences.zh: 擒翦東吳，則訏謨廊廟之輔。

translations.literal: when eastern Wu was captured, he was counselor in the hall of state.
translations.idiomatic: when eastern Wu was captured, he stood as counselor in the hall of state.

sentences.zh: 較其功則有異，言其力則不倫。

translations.literal: Compare achievements and they differ; speak of strength and they are not of a kind.
translations.idiomatic: Compare achievements and they differ; speak of strength and they are not alike.

sentences.zh: 何舍其所重而錄其所輕，收其所小而略其所大？

translations.literal: Why set aside what is weighty and record what is light, gather the small and omit the great?
translations.idiomatic: Why discard what is weighty and record what is light, gather the small and pass over the great?

sentences.zh: 且奢靡是嗜，而曰愛人以儉；

translations.literal: And he loved extravagance yet said he cherished people through frugality;
translations.idiomatic: He loved extravagance yet claimed to cherish the people through frugality;

sentences.zh: 受授無守，而曰慎才以補。

translations.literal: he accepted office without holding to it yet said he chose talent carefully to fill posts.
translations.idiomatic: he accepted office without holding to it yet claimed to choose talent carefully for each post.

sentences.zh: 斥諫諍之士於外，豈不近之蔽聰乎？

translations.literal: Driving remonstrating scholars outside—is this not blinding the ears nearby?
translations.idiomatic: Driving remonstrating scholars outside—is this not blinding the ears of the ruler nearby?

sentences.zh: 舉忠烈之廟於內，豈不近之昵愛也？

translations.literal: Raising shrines to loyal martyrs within—is this not favoring intimates nearby?
translations.idiomatic: Raising shrines to loyal martyrs within—is this not favoring intimates at court?

sentences.zh: 焉有蔽聰昵愛，家範無制，而能垂法作程，憲章百度乎？

translations.literal: How can blinding the ears and favoring intimates, with no discipline in the family model, still set law as standard and regulate the hundred measures?
translations.idiomatic: How can blinding the ears, favoring intimates, and lacking discipline in the family model still set law as standard and regulate the hundred measures?

sentences.zh: 謹按謚法，敬以直內，內而不肅，何以刑於外？

translations.literal: I respectfully consult the posthumous norms: "Reverent" means upright within; if within is not solemn, how govern without?
translations.idiomatic: I respectfully consult the posthumous norms: "Reverent" means upright within; if within is not solemn, how can one govern without?

sentences.zh: 憲者，法也。

translations.literal: "Lawful" means law.
translations.idiomatic: "Lawful" means law itself.

sentences.zh: 《戴記》曰：「憲章文武。」

translations.literal: The Record of Rites says: "Take the laws and models of Wen and Wu."
translations.idiomatic: The Record of Rites says: "Take the laws and models of King Wen and King Wu."

sentences.zh: 又曰：「發慮憲。」

translations.literal: It also says: "Raise plans with law."
translations.idiomatic: It also says: "Form plans with law in mind."

sentences.zh: 義以為敬恪終始，載考歷位，未嘗效一法官，議一小獄。

translations.literal: By "respectful" I mean reverent from start to finish; examining his successive offices, he never once acted as a judge or deliberated a minor case.
translations.idiomatic: By "respectful" I mean reverent from start to finish; examining his successive offices, he never once acted as judge or deliberated even a minor case.

sentences.zh: 及居重位，以安和平易寬柔自處。

translations.literal: When he held heavy rank he rested in ease, peace, and softness.
translations.idiomatic: When he held heavy rank he rested in ease, peace, and softness alone.

sentences.zh: 考其名，與其行不類；

translations.literal: Examining the name against the conduct, they do not match;
translations.idiomatic: Weigh the name against the conduct, and they do not match;

sentences.zh: 研其事，與其道不侔。

translations.literal: studying the deeds against the Way, they are not alike.
translations.idiomatic: studying the deeds against the Way—they are not alike.

sentences.zh: 一定之辭，惟精惟審，異日詳制，貽諸史官。

translations.literal: A fixed phrase, refined and examined—with a detailed regulation another day left to the historians.
translations.idiomatic: Let the phrase be fixed, refined and examined—with detailed regulation left to the historians on another day.

sentences.zh: 請俟蔡寇將平，天下無事，然後都堂聚議，謚亦未遲。

translations.literal: Please wait until the Cai bandits are nearly pacified and the realm is at peace; then the chief ministers may gather in council—the posthumous title is not yet late.
translations.idiomatic: Please wait until the Cai bandits are nearly pacified and the realm is at peace; then the chief ministers may gather in council—the posthumous title need not be rushed.

sentences.zh: 憲宗方用兵，惡仲方深言其事，怒甚，貶為遂州司馬，量移復州司馬。

translations.literal: Emperor Xianzong was then campaigning; he hated Zhongfang's blunt words on the matter and was greatly angered, demoting him to secretary in Suizhou and later transferring him to secretary in Fuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xianzong was then on campaign; he hated Zhongfang's blunt words on the matter, flew into a rage, and demoted him to secretary in Suizhou, later transferring him to secretary in Fuzhou.

sentences.zh: 遷河東少尹。

translations.literal: He was promoted to vice governor of Hedong.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to vice governor of Hedong.

sentences.zh: 未幾，拜鄭州刺史。

translations.literal: Before long he was made prefect of Zhengzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Not long after he was appointed prefect of Zhengzhou.

sentences.zh: 滎陽大海佛寺，有高祖為隋鄭州刺史日，為太宗疾祈福，於此寺造石像一軀，凡刊勒十六字以誌之。

translations.literal: At the Dahai Buddhist Temple in Xingyang there was a stone image that Gaozu, when prefect of Zhengzhou under Sui, had made to pray for Taizong's illness; sixteen characters were carved to record it.
translations.idiomatic: At the Dahai Buddhist Temple in Xingyang stood a stone image that Gaozu, while prefect of Zhengzhou under Sui, had made to pray for Taizong's illness; sixteen characters were carved to record it.

sentences.zh: 歲久剚缺，滎陽令李光慶重加修飾，仲方再刊石記之以聞。

translations.literal: After long years the inscription was chipped away; Magistrate Li Guangqing restored it, and Zhongfang carved the stone record anew and reported it.
translations.idiomatic: After many years the inscription had chipped away; magistrate Li Guangqing restored it, and Zhongfang recarved the stone record and reported it.

sentences.zh: 及敬宗即位，李程作相，與仲方同年登進士第，召仲方為右諫議大夫。

translations.literal: When Emperor Jingzong took the throne, Li Cheng became chief minister; he and Zhongfang had passed the examinations in the same year, and Zhongfang was summoned as Right Remonstrance and Policy Advisor.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Jingzong took the throne, Li Cheng became chief minister; he and Zhongfang had passed the examinations in the same year, and Zhongfang was summoned as right remonstrance and policy advisor.

sentences.zh: 敬宗童年戲慢，詔淮南王播造上巳競渡船三十只。

translations.literal: Jingzong in youth was playful and disrespectful; an edict ordered Prince of Huainan Wang Bo to build thirty dragon-boat racing vessels for the Upper Si festival.
translations.idiomatic: Jingzong in youth was playful and disrespectful; an edict ordered the Prince of Huainan, Wang Bo, to build thirty dragon-boat racing vessels for the Upper Si festival.

sentences.zh: 播將船材於京師造作，計用半年轉運之費方得成。

translations.literal: Bo would fashion the timber in the capital; it was calculated that half a year's transport costs would be needed before they could be completed.
translations.idiomatic: Bo would fashion the timber in the capital; it was estimated that half a year's transport costs would be required before completion.

sentences.zh: 仲方詣延英面論，言甚懇激。

translations.literal: Zhongfang went to Yanying and argued face to face, his words earnest and impassioned.
translations.idiomatic: Zhongfang went to Yanying and argued face to face—his words earnest and impassioned.

sentences.zh: 帝只令造十只以進。

translations.literal: The emperor ordered only ten built for presentation.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor ordered only ten vessels built for presentation.

sentences.zh: 帝又欲幸華清宮，仲方諫曰：「萬乘所幸，出須備儀。

translations.literal: The emperor also wished to visit Huaqing Palace; Zhongfang remonstrated: "Where the imperial carriage goes, escort must be complete.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor also wished to visit Huaqing Palace—Zhongfang remonstrated: "Where the imperial carriage goes, escort must be complete.

sentences.zh: 無宜輕行，以失威重。」

translations.literal: One should not travel lightly and lose majesty."
translations.idiomatic: One should not travel lightly and thereby lose majesty."

sentences.zh: 帝雖不從，慰勞之。

translations.literal: Though the emperor did not follow him, he comforted and praised him.
translations.idiomatic: Though the emperor did not follow his advice, he comforted and praised him.

sentences.zh: 太和初，出為福州刺史、兼御史中丞、福建觀察使。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Taihe he went out as prefect of Fuzhou and concurrent Vice Censor-in-Chief, Fujian observation commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Taihe he went out as prefect of Fuzhou and concurrent vice censor-in-chief, Fujian observation commissioner.

sentences.zh: 三年，入為太子賓客。

translations.literal: In the third year he entered court as Grand Mentor of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year he entered court as grand mentor of the heir apparent.

sentences.zh: 五年四月，轉右散騎常侍。

translations.literal: In the fourth month of the fifth year he was transferred to Right Regular Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month of the fifth year he was transferred to right regular attendant.

sentences.zh: 七年，李德裕輔政，出為太子賓客分司。

translations.literal: In the seventh year, with Li Deyu aiding governance, he was sent out as Grand Mentor of the Heir Apparent in honorary service.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year, with Li Deyu aiding governance, he was sent out as grand mentor of the heir apparent in honorary service.

sentences.zh: 八年，德裕罷相，李守閔復召仲方為常侍。

translations.literal: In the eighth year, when Deyu left the chief ministry, Li Shoumin again summoned Zhongfang as regular attendant.
translations.idiomatic: During the eighth year, when Deyu left the chief ministry, Li Shoumin again summoned Zhongfang as regular attendant.

sentences.zh: 九年十一月，李訓之亂，四宰相、中丞、京兆尹皆死。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month of the ninth year, in Li Xun's rebellion, four chief ministers, the censor-in-chief, and the Jingzhao governor all died.
translations.idiomatic: During the eleventh month of the ninth year, in Li Xun's rebellion, four chief ministers, the censor-in-chief, and the Jingzhao governor all died.

sentences.zh: 翌日，兩省官入朝。

translations.literal: The next day, officials of the two departments entered court.
translations.idiomatic: On the following day, officials of the two departments entered court.

sentences.zh: 宣政衙門未開，百官錯立於朝堂，無人吏引接。

translations.literal: The Xuanzheng gate was not yet open; officials stood confused in the court hall with no clerks to guide them.
translations.idiomatic: The Xuanzheng gate was not yet open—officials stood confused in the court hall with no clerks to guide them.

sentences.zh: 逡巡，閣門使馬元贄斜開宣政衙門傳宣曰：「有敕召左散騎常侍張仲方。」

translations.literal: After a while, Gate Commissioner Ma Yuanzan partly opened the Xuanzheng gate and proclaimed: "There is an edict summoning Left Regular Attendant Zhang Zhongfang."
translations.idiomatic: After a while, gate commissioner Ma Yuanzan partly opened the Xuanzheng gate and proclaimed: "There is an edict summoning left regular attendant Zhang Zhongfang."

sentences.zh: 仲方出班。

translations.literal: Zhongfang stepped from the ranks.
translations.idiomatic: Zhongfang stepped forward from the ranks.

sentences.zh: 元贄宣曰：「仲方可京兆尹。」

translations.literal: Yuanzan proclaimed: "Zhongfang may be Jingzhao governor."
translations.idiomatic: Yuanzan proclaimed: "Zhongfang is appointed Jingzhao governor."

sentences.zh: 然後衙門大開，喚仗。

translations.literal: Only then were the gates fully opened and the guard called.
translations.idiomatic: Only then were the gates thrown fully open and the guard summoned.

sentences.zh: 月余，鄭覃作相，用薛元賞為京兆尹，出仲方為華州刺史。

translations.literal: After a little more than a month, Zheng Tan became chief minister; he used Xue Yuanshang as Jingzhao governor and sent Zhongfang out as prefect of Huazhou.
translations.idiomatic: Following a little more than a month, Zheng Tan became chief minister; he used Xue Yuanshang as Jingzhao governor and sent Zhongfang out as prefect of Huazhou.

sentences.zh: 開成元年五月，入為秘書監。

translations.literal: In the fifth month of the first year of Kaicheng he entered court as Director of the Palace Library.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month of the first year of Kaicheng he entered court as director of the palace library.

sentences.zh: 外議以鄭覃黨李德裕，排擯仲方。

translations.literal: Outside opinion held that Zheng Tan, partisan to Li Deyu, had squeezed Zhongfang out.
translations.idiomatic: Outside opinion held that Zheng Tan, partisan to Li Deyu—had squeezed Zhongfang out.

sentences.zh: 覃恐涉朋黨，因紫宸奏事，覃啟曰：「丞郎闕人，臣欲用張仲方。」

translations.literal: Tan feared the appearance of faction, and while reporting affairs at Zichen said: "Vice directors are vacant; I wish to use Zhang Zhongfang."
translations.idiomatic: Tan feared the appearance of faction, and while reporting affairs at Zichen said: "Vice directors are vacant—I wish to use Zhang Zhongfang."

sentences.zh: 文宗曰：「中臺侍郎，朝廷華選。

translations.literal: Emperor Wenzong said: "Vice director in the Secretariat is a splendid court selection.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wenzong said: "A vice director in the Secretariat is a splendid court appointment.

sentences.zh: 仲方作牧守無政，安可以丞郎處之？」

translations.literal: As prefect Zhongfang had no good governance—how can he be placed as vice director?"
translations.idiomatic: As prefect, Zhongfang showed no good governance—how can he be placed as vice director?"

sentences.zh: 累加銀青光祿大夫、上柱國、曲江縣開國伯，食邑七百戶。

translations.literal: He was repeatedly given Silver and Blue Glory Grand Master of the Palace, Upper Pillar of the State, Baron of Qujiang with a fief of seven hundred households.
translations.idiomatic: He was repeatedly given silver and blue glory grand master of the palace, upper pillar of the state, baron of Qujiang with a fief of seven hundred households.

sentences.zh: 二年四月卒。

translations.literal: In the fourth month of the second year he died.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the fourth month of the second year.

sentences.zh: 仲方貞確自立，綽有祖風。

translations.literal: Zhongfang was upright and self-reliant, with ample ancestral bearing.
translations.idiomatic: Zhongfang was upright and self-reliant—with ample ancestral bearing.

sentences.zh: 自駁謚之後，為德裕之黨擯斥，坎坷而歿，人士輩之。

translations.literal: After the posthumous-title rebuttal he was driven out by Deyu's faction and died in hardship; men of the age pitied him.
translations.idiomatic: Following the posthumous-title rebuttal he was driven out by Deyu's faction and died in hardship; men of the age pitied him.

sentences.zh: 有文集三十卷。

translations.literal: He had a collected writings in thirty scrolls.
translations.idiomatic: He had collected writings in thirty scrolls.

sentences.zh: 兄仲端，位終都昌令。

translations.literal: His elder brother Zhongduan ended as magistrate of Duchang.
translations.idiomatic: His elder brother Zhongduan ended his career as magistrate of Duchang.

sentences.zh: 弟仲孚，登進士第，為監察御史。

translations.literal: His younger brother Zhongfu passed the civil examinations and became investigating censor.
translations.idiomatic: His younger brother Zhongfu earned his jinshi degree and became investigating censor.

sentences.zh: 裴潾，河東人也。

translations.literal: Pei Lin was a man of Hedong.
translations.idiomatic: Pei Lin came from Hedong.

sentences.zh: 少篤學，善隸書。

translations.literal: From youth he studied earnestly and was skilled at clerical script.
translations.idiomatic: From youth he applied himself to study and excelled at clerical script.

sentences.zh: 以門廕入仕。

translations.literal: He entered office through hereditary privilege.
translations.idiomatic: He took office by hereditary privilege.

sentences.zh: 元和初，累遷右拾遺，轉左補闕。

translations.literal: In the early Yuanhe era he was promoted repeatedly to Right Reminder and transferred to Left Supplementation Omission.
translations.idiomatic: In the early Yuanhe era he was promoted repeatedly to right reminder and transferred to left supplementation omission.

sentences.zh: 元和中，兩河用兵。

translations.literal: In the Yuanhe era the two He regions were at war.
translations.idiomatic: During the Yuanhe era the two He regions were at war.

sentences.zh: 初，憲宗寵任內官，有至專兵柄者，又以內官充館驛使。

translations.literal: Earlier Emperor Xianzong had favored inner officials, some even monopolizing military power, and also used inner officials as postal relay commissioners.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier Emperor Xianzong had favored inner officials, some even monopolizing military power—and also used inner officials as postal relay commissioners.

sentences.zh: 有曹進玉者，恃恩暴戾，遇四方使多倨，有至捽辱者，宰相李吉甫奏罷之。

translations.literal: One Cao Jinyu, relying on favor, was violent and arrogant; he treated envoys from the four directions with much haughtiness, sometimes seizing and insulting them; Chief Minister Li Jifu memorialized to abolish the post.
translations.idiomatic: One Cao Jinyu, relying on favor, was violent and arrogant; he treated envoys from the four directions with much haughtiness, sometimes seizing and insulting them; chief minister Li Jifu memorialized to abolish the post.

sentences.zh: 十二年，淮西用兵，復以內官為使。

translations.literal: In the twelfth year, with war in Huai west, inner officials were again used as commissioners.
translations.idiomatic: During the twelfth year, with war in Huai west, inner officials were again used as commissioners.

sentences.zh: 潾上疏曰：「館驛之務，每驛皆有專知官。

translations.literal: Lin submitted a memorial saying: "In postal relay affairs each station has its dedicated officer.
translations.idiomatic: Lin submitted a memorial in which he wrote: "In postal relay affairs each station has its dedicated officer.

sentences.zh: 畿內有京兆尹，外道有觀察使、刺史叠相監臨；

translations.literal: Within the capital circuit there is the Jingzhao governor; outside there are observation commissioners and prefects overseeing in layers;
translations.idiomatic: Within the capital circuit there is the Jingzhao governor—outside there are observation commissioners and prefects overseeing in layers;

sentences.zh: 臺中又有御史充館驛使，專察過闕。

translations.literal: within the censorate there are also censors serving as postal commissioners, specializing in inspecting faults.
translations.idiomatic: within the censorate there are also censors serving as postal commissioners—specializing in inspecting faults.

sentences.zh: 伏知近有敗事，上聞聖聰。

translations.literal: I know lately there have been failures reported to Your Sacred Ears.
translations.idiomatic: I know that lately there have been failures reported to Your Sacred Ears.

sentences.zh: 但明示科條，督責官吏，據其所犯，重加貶黜，敢不惕懼，日夜厲精。

translations.literal: But clearly show the statutes, supervise and hold officials accountable, and according to their offenses heavily demote them—they will not fail to be wary, toiling day and night with diligence.
translations.idiomatic: But clearly show the statutes, supervise and hold officials accountable, and according to their offenses heavily demote them—they will not fail to be wary—toiling day and night with diligence.

sentences.zh: 若令宮闈之臣，出參館驛之務，則內臣外事，職分各殊，切在塞侵官之源，絕出位之漸。

translations.literal: If palace persons are sent to join postal relay duties, then inner officials in outer affairs—each office distinct—urgently block the source of encroaching office and cut off the first step beyond one's place.
translations.idiomatic: If palace persons are sent to join postal relay duties, then inner officials will meddle in outer affairs—each office has its own sphere; we must urgently block the source of encroachment and cut off the first step beyond one's place.

sentences.zh: 事有不便，必誡以初；

translations.literal: When affairs are inconvenient, warn as at the start;
translations.idiomatic: Once affairs are inconvenient, warn as at the start;

sentences.zh: 令或有妨，不必在大。

translations.literal: if orders have hindrances, it need not be on a grand scale.
translations.idiomatic: if an order meets hindrance, the warning need not be made on a grand scale.

sentences.zh: 當掃靜妖氛之日，開太平至理之風。

translations.literal: When sweeping away demonic mists, open the wind of supreme peace and perfect order.
translations.idiomatic: Once sweeping away demonic mists, open the wind of supreme peace and perfect order.

sentences.zh: 澄本正名，實在今日。」

translations.literal: Clarifying the root and rectifying names—in truth lies in today."
translations.idiomatic: To clarify the root and rectify names—the truth of the matter lies in what we do today."

sentences.zh: 言雖不用，帝意嘉之，遷起居舍人。

translations.literal: Though the words were not adopted, the emperor was pleased and promoted him to Diarist.
translations.idiomatic: Though the words were not adopted, the emperor was pleased and promoted him to diarist.

sentences.zh: 憲宗季年銳於服餌，詔天下搜訪奇士。

translations.literal: In Xianzong's late years he was keen on elixirs; an edict ordered the realm to search for extraordinary men.
translations.idiomatic: In Xianzong's late years he was keen on elixirs—an edict ordered the realm to search for extraordinary men.

sentences.zh: 宰相皇甫镈與金吾將軍李道古挾邪固寵，薦山人柳泌及僧大通、鳳翔人田佐元，皆待詔翰林。

translations.literal: Chief Minister Huangfu Bo and Gold Crow guard general Li Daogu, clutching evil to secure favor, recommended the mountain man Liu Bi and the monk Datong and Fengxiang man Tian Zuoyuan—all awaited edicts in the Hanlin.
translations.idiomatic: Chief Minister Huangfu Bo and Gold Crow Guard general Li Daogu, clutching evil to secure favor, recommended the mountain recluse Liu Bi, the monk Datong, and Tian Zuoyuan of Fengxiang—all were retained at the Hanlin Academy.

sentences.zh: 憲宗服泌藥，日增躁渴，流聞於外。

translations.literal: Xianzong took Bi's medicine and daily grew restless and thirsty; word spread outside.
translations.idiomatic: Xianzong took Bi's medicine and daily grew restless and thirsty—word spread outside.

sentences.zh: 潾上疏諫曰：

translations.literal: Lin submitted a remonstrance memorial saying:
translations.idiomatic: Lin submitted a remonstrance memorial in which he wrote:

sentences.zh: 臣聞除天下之害者，受天下之利；

translations.literal: I have heard that one who removes the realm's harms receives the realm's benefits;
translations.idiomatic: I have heard said that one who removes the realm's harms receives the realm's benefits;

sentences.zh: 共天下之樂者，饗天下之福。

translations.literal: one who shares the realm's joys enjoys the realm's blessings.
translations.idiomatic: who shares the realm's joys will enjoy the realm's blessings.

sentences.zh: 故上自黃帝、顓頊、堯、舜、禹、湯，下及周文王、武王，鹹以功濟生靈，德配天地，故天皆報之以上壽，垂祚於無疆。

translations.literal: Thus from above Huangdi, Zhuanxu, Yao, Shun, Yu, and Tang, down to King Wen and King Wu of Zhou—all by merit succored the living, virtue matching heaven and earth—heaven therefore repaid them with long life and endless succession.
translations.idiomatic: Thus from above Huangdi, Zhuanxu, Yao, Shun, Yu, and Tang, down to King Wen and King Wu of Zhou—all by merit succored the living—virtue matching heaven and earth—heaven therefore repaid them with long life and endless succession.

sentences.zh: 伏見陛下以大孝安宗廟，以至仁牧黎元。

translations.literal: I see Your Majesty with great filial piety settling the ancestral temple and with utmost benevolence shepherding the black-haired people.
translations.idiomatic: I observe Your Majesty with great filial piety settling the ancestral temple and with utmost benevolence shepherding the black-haired people.

sentences.zh: 自踐祚已來，刬積代之妖兇，開削平之洪業。

translations.literal: Since taking the throne you have cut away age-old demons and opened the grand enterprise of pacification.
translations.idiomatic: Since you took the throne you have cut away age-old demons and opened the grand enterprise of pacification.

sentences.zh: 而禮敬宰輔，待以終始；

translations.literal: Yet you honor chief ministers and treat them with constancy from start to finish;
translations.idiomatic: And yet you honor chief ministers and treat them with constancy from start to finish;

sentences.zh: 內能大斷，外寬小故。

translations.literal: within you decide greatly, without you are lenient on small faults.
translations.idiomatic: within, you decide greatly; without, you are lenient toward small faults.

sentences.zh: 夫此神功聖化，皆自古聖主明君所不及，陛下躬親行之，實光映千古矣。

translations.literal: This divine merit and sage transformation—all that ancient sage rulers could not reach—Your Majesty personally performs; it truly shines across a thousand ages.
